scenes.heading: Percentages and money
scenes.say: Every receipt, sale sign and pay rise uses percentages. In this lesson you'll handle GST, discounts, mark-ups and profit with one simple tool: the multiplier.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Any amount is a pizza cut into 100 slices
scenes.science: 20% off: pay for 80 slices. GST: pay for 110
scenes.breaks: After a discount the pizza is smaller, so the next percentage is a slice of a smaller pizza.
scenes.say: Per cent means out of one hundred. Picture any amount as a pizza cut into a hundred slices. Twenty per cent off means you pay for eighty slices. GST adds ten more, so you pay for one hundred and ten. But after a discount the pizza is smaller, so the next percentage is a slice of a smaller pizza.

scenes.heading: Multipliers
scenes.say: Start at one hundred per cent. To add GST, times one point one. Twenty-five per cent off leaves seventy-five, so times point seven five. A forty-five per cent mark-up is times one point four five. And to find the GST hiding inside a price, divide by eleven.
scenes.caption: Start at 100%. Add GST: × 1.1. 25% off: × 0.75. A 45% mark-up: × 1.45. To find the GST inside a price, divide by 11.

scenes.heading: Adding GST
scenes.say: Here's GST as a bar. First the bar for the price before GST, two hundred dollars, which is one hundred per cent. Then a small piece for GST, ten per cent of two hundred, or twenty dollars. Altogether, one hundred and ten per cent: two hundred and twenty dollars.
scenes.caption: The price before GST, $200, is 100%. GST adds 10% of $200 = $20. Altogether 110%: $220.

scenes.heading: Finding the GST
scenes.question: A helmet costs $154 including GST. Find the GST and the price before GST.
scenes.say: A helmet costs a hundred and fifty-four dollars including GST. That's one hundred and ten per cent. Split it into eleven equal parts of ten per cent. The GST is one of them, so divide by eleven: fourteen dollars. The price before GST is one hundred and forty. Ten per cent of a hundred and fifty-four is the classic trap.
scenes.caption: A helmet costs $154 including GST. That is 110%. GST = 154 ÷ 11 = $14. The price before GST is $140. Taking 10% of $154 is the classic trap.

scenes.heading: Mark-up, then a sale
scenes.question: Cost $60, marked up 45%, then 20% off. Find the percentage profit.
scenes.say: A shop buys a kettle for sixty dollars and marks it up forty-five per cent: eighty-seven dollars. Then twenty per cent off: sixty-nine dollars sixty. The profit is nine dollars sixty. Divide by the cost price, sixty, to get a sixteen per cent profit.
scenes.caption: Cost $60, marked up 45%: $87. Then 20% off: $69.60. Profit $9.60. Divide by the cost price: 16% profit.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Part over whole, times one hundred, gives a percentage. Add GST by multiplying by one point one, and find it by dividing by eleven. Use multipliers for discounts and mark-ups. Profit percentage is always over the cost price. Now try the practice questions!
